narrative:
The model determined that you have a 34% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were the loan amount you requested, the status of your checking account, and how long you have lived at your current address. 

Your requested loan amount of 2,039 DM was noticeably smaller than the average amount approved applicants ask for (about 3,020 DM). This smaller request worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward good credit. However, two other important factors pushed strongly in the opposite direction. Your checking account shows a balance between 0 and 200 DM, a situation that is relatively uncommon among approved applicants and signaled higher risk to the model. In addition, having lived at your present residence for only one year is shorter than the typical approved applicant, and this also increased the predicted risk.

Taken together, the negative signals from your checking account status and short time at your current address outweighed the positive effect of the smaller loan amount, leading to the denial.

You should focus on building a stronger checking account balance and staying at one address for a longer period. Once those areas improve, reapply. You may also want to explore smaller loans or alternative lenders in the meantime. (218 words)
